title: Souza's Conjecture on Blowup Ramsey Numbers
statement_text: In the bound $B(G \xrightarrow{r} H; t) \leq c^t$, the exponential constant $c$ can be chosen to depend only on $H$ and $r$, and not on $G$.
context_text: Souza introduced blowup Ramsey numbers and proved $B(G \xrightarrow{r} H; t) \leq c(G,H,r)^t$. He conjectured that the dependence on $G$ in the exponential constant is unnecessary, motivated by the fact that his lower bound constant $c'$ already does not depend on $G$.
paper_contribution: Proves Theorem 2: $B(G \xrightarrow{r} H; t) \leq a \cdot b^t$ where $b = b(H,r)$ is independent of $G$, confirming that the exponential growth rate does not depend on $G$.
paper_title: Extremal and Ramsey results on graph blowups

title: Conjecture on unavoidable G-dependence in Theorem 2
statement_text: For some graph $H$, the dependence on $G$ in the multiplicative factor $a = a(G, H, r)$ of the bound $B(G \xrightarrow{r} H; t) \leq a \cdot b^t$ (proved by the authors with $b=b(H,r)$ independent of $G$) is unavoidable. Precisely: there exist a graph $H$ and integers $r,t\ge2$, and graphs $G_1,G_2,\ldots$ such that $G_i\xrightarrow{r}H$ for all $i$ and $\sup_i B(G_i\xrightarrow{r}H;t)=\infty$.
context_text: $G\xrightarrow{r}H$ means that every $r$-edge-colouring of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. The $t$-blowup $H[t]$ is obtained by replacing each vertex of $H$ by an independent set of size $t$ and each edge by a complete bipartite graph $K_{t,t}$; a copy of $H[t]$ in $G[n]$ is canonical if it is the $t$-blowup of a copy of $H$ in $G$. For $G\xrightarrow{r}H$, the blowup Ramsey number $B(G\xrightarrow{r}H;t)$, introduced by Souza, is the least $n$ such that every $r$-edge-colouring of $G[n]$ contains a monochromatic canonical copy of $H[t]$. Souza proved $B(G\xrightarrow{r}H;t)\le c^t$ with $c=c(G,H,r)$, and a lower bound exponential in $t$ with a constant independent of $G$, and conjectured that the dependence on $G$ is unnecessary. The authors prove $B(G\xrightarrow{r}H;t)\le a\cdot b^t$ with $a=a(G,H,r)$ and $b=b(H,r)$, so the exponential rate does not depend on $G$, but, unlike Souza, they believe the prefactor must depend on $G$ for some $H$, and even conjecture this for $H=K_3$, $r=t=2$: for every $s$ there is $G$ with $G\xrightarrow{2}K_3$ but $G[s]\not\xrightarrow{2}K_3[2]$. Such an $H$ cannot be $r$-Ramsey-finite (having finitely many minimal $G$ with $G\xrightarrow{r}H$), and $H=P_3$, the path with two edges, does not work for $r=2$ although it is Ramsey-infinite: then $B(G\xrightarrow{2}P_3;t)\le c^t$ with $c$ absolute.
notes: Stated in both the abstract and the introduction as a belief/conjecture without a labelled theorem environment; concluding remarks section was not fully captured in the PDF extraction.
paper_title: Extremal and Ramsey results on graph blowups
